findings.title: D4's move of the bundled `analysis` agents skills out of `commands/agents/` breaks 925's drift guard, and the design never reconciles it
findings.description:
D4 moves `commands/agents/analysis-understand/` and `commands/agents/analysis-tech-debt-audit/` into `commands/analysis/agents/` so the bundled pack's source resolves to `commands/analysis` and D2 applies. That is fine for the *Claude* consumers the design actually checked: I confirmed the Claude writers (`installer._install_prefix` globs `source_path.glob("*.md")` top-level) and `metrology/audit.py::resolve_audit_skill` (reads `pack_dir / "tech-debt-audit.md"` top-level) do not recurse, so the new subdirectory is invisible to them, as D4 claims.

But the design does not examine 925's **drift guard** in `tests/cli/test_install_commands.py`, which is a shipped CI test enforcing a bijection between the two asset trees, and the move breaks it:

- `test_every_claude_command_has_an_agents_twin` builds expected paths from `DELIVERIES[CLAUDE].bundle_subdirs` (`("sq", "analysis")`), so for `commands/analysis/understand.md` it asserts `commands/agents/analysis-understand/SKILL.md` exists (`_agents_root()` is hard-wired to `get_commands_source() / "agents"`). After the move that file lives at `commands/analysis/agents/analysis-understand/SKILL.md`, so the assertion fails.
- `test_openai_yaml_mirrors_disable_model_invocation` iterates the same `_claude_twins()` and asserts `commands/agents/analysis-understand/agents/openai.yaml` — also gone after the move.
- `test_every_agents_skill_has_a_claude_twin` / `test_agents_skill_name_matches_its_directory` will now pass only by accident (the analysis skills are no longer under `commands/agents/`), silently *narrowing* the guard's coverage of the two analysis skills rather than continuing to protect them.

The requirement left unmet is that 925's drift bijection (a success criterion of 925 and the only thing making Claude↔agents divergence loud) must remain green and meaningful. The design must state how the guard reconciles once the bundled analysis pack's agents content splits out of `commands/agents/` — e.g. does `_agents_root()`/the `required` set now read `commands/analysis/agents/` for analysis skills and `commands/agents/` for `sq-*`, or are the analysis skills deliberately exempted from the guard (and why)?

Compounding this, the **Migration Plan** claims "Existing tests for those commands pass without edits other than the moved fixture paths." That is incorrect for the drift tests: they encode structural bijection logic over the real bundle, not a fixture path to repoint, so they require logic changes, not path edits. The plan should name the guard explicitly and correct that sentence, or an implementer reading it will either ship a red build or weaken the guard without realizing it.

findings.title: Dependency direction and the 925 integration contract are respected
findings.description: 928 depends only on 925 (complete), which is the correct direction (928 → 925, both under 900). It consumes precisely the surface 925's "Provides to Other Slices" promised for "the follow-up skill-pack targeting work" — `CommandTarget`, `normalize_target`, `DELIVERIES`, `write_skill_dirs`, and doctor's target selection — and reuses it "unchanged in meaning" as 925's Integration Points require. I verified D5's generalization against `targets.py`: today's four receipt names (`squadron-commands`, `-local`, `-agents`, `-agents-local`) and a Claude machine pack install (`<pack>.toml`) are reproduced exactly by `receipt_name(base, target, *, local)` with bases `""`/`"-agents"`, so there is genuinely no receipt migration, matching the design's claim.

findings.title: New agents install I/O path has enumerated failure modes with explicit handling
findings.description: The one genuinely new I/O path (agents-target pack install) has its failure modes handled explicitly rather than left implicit: pack with no `agents/` directory → `SkillSourceError`, exit 1, nothing written (D2, criterion 3, walkthrough step 3); any D3 name/frontmatter violation → all violations collected and reported together, nothing written unless all pass; `agents/` present but empty → error, not an empty install; nested-skill uninstall → shared `remove_receipt_files` prunes deepest-first, never the destination, never a file outside it (D7); no receipt → "not installed," removes nothing (inherited). The github-source clone path is correctly marked "unchanged" (it already raises `SkillSourceError` via `clone_github`). This directly delivers the stated Value that a pack with no Codex content "fails loudly instead of installing somewhere inert."
